name: Living with Your Partner (Unmarried Partner Permit)

qualifying_event.description: An unmarried foreign partner of an Aruban-born Dutch national may apply for a residence permit to live with that partner, where the sponsor guarantees support and meets the income test.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Deed of registered partnership (from a European Dutch Kingdom area or BES island) or a notarial partnership deed from an Aruba-registered notary; proof of cohabitation at the same address.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires a long-term, exclusive, unmarried relationship with a partner of a different gender who holds Dutch nationality and was born in Aruba, with both partners cohabiting at the same address.
The sponsoring partner must sign as guarantor and earn an annual income at or above the Aruban CBS (Central Bureau of Statistics) minimum wage norm.
Requires private health insurance for one year (exempt for EU and US citizens).

evidence_required.document: Deed of registered partnership or notarial partnership deed
Sponsorship statement and proof of sponsor's income
Proof of private health insurance (unless EU/US citizen)

sources.title: DIMAS, Government of Aruba -- Living with Your Partner: unmarried-partner permit requiring the Dutch-national sponsor to have been born in Aruba, a different-gender relationship, CBS minimum-wage sponsor income test, 1-year renewable permit, registered-partnership deed requirement

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Aruba's initial build. This is a distinct, narrower route from aw_family_reunification.json: the DIMAS source page states this permit requires the sponsoring partner to be of a DIFFERENT GENDER from the applicant and to be a Dutch national specifically born in Aruba (not merely any Dutch national or resident) -- both stated plainly on the official page and reported here factually as the eligibility rule DIMAS itself publishes, not a judgment this dataset makes. Same-sex partners and partners of Dutch nationals not born in Aruba are not covered by this specific route per the source reviewed; no equivalent DIMAS route for those situations was found in this pass, which is flagged here as an open gap rather than assumed not to exist. leads_to_pr is not modelled since the page gives no path beyond annual renewal; a holder who marries the sponsor could potentially move to aw_family_reunification.json's married-sponsor ground instead, though that switch was not explicitly confirmed on either page.
